_about: The gaps the gauntlet asserts. Each row is one component, the verified vault file it is held
against, the figure read off that file's frames in vault/SPECS.md, and a measurement of the
app's own specimen that has to come out the same way.
A row without `assert` is honest about being a caution or a counter-example: the sheet shows
it, the run prints it, and nobody is allowed to call it a pass.
test/gauntlet.test.mjs refuses a row naming a file the eye never verified, a component that
is not in the registry, or a figure that is not the one SPECS.md measured.

gaps.referenceFigure: measured: 48 frames over 8.0s, no bright marker crosses the frame
gaps.gap: In the audio editor the waveform exists as ink along a named lane and the ONLY thing that moves is a marker crossing an axis already fully drawn — ruler, labels and selection block hold still. A component that grows its own series into being is animating the data instead of reading it, so the library's series must arrive and then hold.

gaps.referenceFigure: measured: 48 frames over 8.0s, motion amplitude (max difference from frame zero): 5.4
gaps.gap: The audio editor's whole idiom is a marker crossing a strip that is ALREADY ink: the waveform, the ruler, the track labels and the selection block hold still and one hairline travels. `tape` has no such marker — it stamps `count`, `elapsed`, `still` and one refusal, and nothing translates along its axis. The five mark kinds that exist cannot express it: `trace` reveals a shape, `count` reveals by index, `cycle` addresses a clock, `level` is an extent from an anchor. Building it means a kind that moves a marker along an axis, which is a library change, not a showcase change.
gaps.notHeld: Two facts, read out of the source rather than the name. `tape` is the DECISION tape -- a queue of waits with an `elapsed` clock on each row and no axis to cross, so there is no position for a marker to have. And the component that DOES draw time, `river`, scales every lane to its own first-and-last event (px(t) normalises by that lane's span), so there is no shared present anywhere in the drawing to put a line on; a now-line clamped to each lane's right edge would say 'now is where this lane stopped', which is the falsest sentence a time chart can make. The idiom needs a shared absolute axis, which the library does not draw.

gaps.referenceFigure: measured: 32 frames over 4.01s, motion amplitude (max difference from frame zero): 15.82
gaps.gap: On the Solari board only the cells whose value changed flip; the destination labels and the column heads never stir, so the movement is the report and everything else is ink. A dispatch panel that animates its own furniture on every refresh says 'everything changed' when one row did, so the furniture must hold still over a change.

gaps.referenceFigure: travel of the bright head: 0.163 of the frame crossed
gaps.gap: A flap has a fixed set of faces and no in-between state to render: it goes from one character to the next, and the low measured centroid travel (0.163, most of it the handheld camera) is the number that says so — a change in place, not a change arriving across the screen. `hardCut` must therefore never be an eased crossfade of the old value into the new.
the loop returns toward its oldest step through a fade or an eased position reset, where the reference wraps in a jump
gaps.referenceFigure: 25 frames over 4.17s, median delay 170.0ms, loop no return to frame zero
gaps.assertKind: a position trace at frame resolution across two periods, checked for a discontinuity at the wrap
gaps.observed: not asserted; the row is recorded so the reference stays attached to the gap it came from
gaps.notHeld: Catching an eased wrap needs the position trace sampled at frame resolution across two full periods and aligned to the wrap. The recorder that does this exists since hardCut was tested, and it taught the harder half of the lesson: a change window about 300ms long is missed entirely by anything sampling at human cadence. Wiring that recorder to a wrap rather than to a click is real work with its own sabotage, and a row written before the sabotage exists would certify the very crossfade it claims to watch for.
gaps.watch: the needle or coverage mass easing back toward zero instead of stepping, or an opacity fade at the wrap

gaps.gap: a wait whose remaining time was never measured is drawn as a progress bar, a percentage, or a remaining-time figure
gaps.referenceFigure: 24 frames over 4.0s, median delay 170.0ms, loop no return to frame zero
gaps.assertKind: an element or number count over the in-flight state: a bar geometry or a % figure must be absent where no duration was supplied
gaps.observed: not asserted; recorded with its reference so the gap keeps the picture it came from
gaps.notHeld: Two hard things, both named rather than papered over. This reference is handheld, so its measured travel belongs to the cameraperson and it can hold a component to a state vocabulary but not to a rate. And the assert needs a specimen whose wait is actually in flight, which the dispatch fixture currently resolves as settled — an assert written now would run against a state nobody renders and could never go red for the reason it exists.
gaps.watch: `dispatch` or `loopDeviation` growing a bar, a percentage, or an ETA without a supplied duration

gaps.gap: lanes are stacked with each lane mapping time by its own normalised position, so a single 'now' has no single x and a playhead or a cross-lane event cannot be drawn
gaps.referenceFigure: 48 frames over 8.0s, median delay 170.0ms, loop no return to frame zero
gaps.assertKind: a geometry read across lanes: for one timestamp, the x of a per-lane marker must be identical in every lane
gaps.observed: not asserted; the gap is the finding and the drawing does not exist yet
gaps.notHeld: An assert cannot fail on a geometry the component never draws. river maps time with px(t) normalised per lane from each lane's own t0 and span, so 'now' resolves to a different x per lane and there is nothing for a cross-lane x assertion to measure; the reference shows one ruler across the whole plate and one playhead over it, which means the fix is a new drawing on an absolute axis rather than a dialect change, and the marker-crossing idiom was already registered as not held for exactly this reason.
gaps.watch: any cross-lane marker, playhead, or 'now' cue added to river — it must land at the same x in every lane, which requires an absolute-time axis the component does not have
